items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I was in college, taking a music course, and we were studying, I forget, Stravinsky or someone.

ctx.x: Where does your inspiration come from for writing new music?

Oh different things. It could be life experiences. I grew up in the church down south, I was in church every Sunday whether I wanted to be or not. I’d really like to do a Gospel album. I recorded a record on Cris Cross called “The Gospel Truth,” which was hymns and spirituals and a couple of original compositions. But it depends. It comes from many things. But mainly things that are blues based and the feeling I guess of the music of the church. And I think it’s intertwined in many different things. And sometimes…

somewhere on the west coast, some small rural town out in the midwest. And one of the themes that he wrote [scats] and on the radio we was listening to a jazz station, we had about twenty minutes to get to the sound check, and a guitarist comes on playing [scats]. I said okay, well the first four measures, well I was just hearing the same thing.
